chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, upon them be peace, said:

Qanbar, the freedman of Ali (peace be upon him), brought his breaking of the fast to him. He said: So he came with a bag containing sawiq (crushed barley flour) with a seal on it. He said: And a man said to him, O Commander of the Faithful, is this not stinginess? You seal your food. He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) smiled. He said: Then he said: And is it not so that I do not like anything to enter my stomach except something whose path I know.

Then he broke the seal, took out the sawiq, put some of it in a cup, and gave it to him. He took the cup, and when he wanted to drink, he said: In the name of God, O God, for You we fasted and upon Your provision we broke the fast, so accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

And what he mentioned in the book of the supplication every day and night, and the explanation of the prayers and the glorification, has already passed in full detail, so there is no reason to repeat it.

key_terms.أَعْرِفُ سَبِيلَهُ: I know its path (referring to knowing the source and purity of the food)
key_terms.سَوِيقٌ: Sawiq, a traditional food made from roasted and ground barley or wheat
key_terms.قَنْبَرٌ: Qanbar, the famous freedman and servant of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when breaking the fast according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) emphasis on *tadqiq* (verification) of sustenance, linking physical purity to spiritual integrity by ensuring the food's source was known and free from doubt. The incident serves as a practical demonstration of mindfulness in worship, where the act of breaking fast is accompanied by a specific du'a affirming God's attributes of hearing and knowledge. This context underscores the Shia scholarly view that ritual acts are deeply intertwined with conscious awareness of divine presence.
